title: Marketplace pilot: commissioning checklist & tile copy
content:
Overview:
This doc is a working playbook for a limited pilot listing of Redwood Inference on cloud marketplaces (beta partners). It's focused on the operational "commissioning" activities required to move a partner from intake -> test tenant -> live tile.

Goal:
Run a tightly scoped pilot with 3 partners to validate conversion of marketplace trials to self-serve signups and to validate billing mapping and telemetry. Key success metrics: trial-to-paid conversion >= 6% in pilot cohort, tile click-to-trial conversion >= 12%, end-to-end provisioning < 30 minutes during tests.

Audience:
Go-to-market ops, partner engineering, product-hosted-api, legal, finance, platform-engineering.

High-level timeline (recommended pilot sprint):
- Week 0: partner intake & contract signatures (legal + finance gating)
- Week 1: sandbox tile copy + visual assets approved, SKU mapping assigned
- Week 2: partnership technical onboarding (SSO test, KMS access, test tenant provisioning)
- Week 3: smoke tests, telemetry validation, billing end-to-end dry run
- Week 4: limited live rollout (1% traffic or single-region listing) + daily check-ins

Commissioning checklist (operational tasks):
- Contract & commercial
  - Confirm commercial terms + pilot duration (default: 60 days).
  - Sign MSA + marketplace addendum (Legal sign-off required).
  - Finance: assign pilot billing SKU and internal revenue code.
- Technical prerequisites
  - Provision test tenant for partner in Hosted test cluster (tenant id & contact).
  - Confirm KMS/HSM access pattern for any customer keys needed.
  - SSO: verify SAML/OIDC test flow if partner requires SSO onboarding.
  - Network: confirm VPC peering endpoints if partner requests private connectivity.
  - Quotas: reserve dedicated capacity or burst tokens if expected QPS > 100.
- Security & compliance
  - Provide SOC2 summary and any applicable audit artifacts to partner security team.
  - Complete minimal pen-test checklist for pilot (list of endpoints reviewed): auth, token issuance, model inference endpoints.
  - Confirm data residency constraints for partner (region and retention).
- Marketplace tile & content
  - Finalize short tile title (<= 60 chars), short description (<= 150 chars), long description (<= 3000 chars).
  - Provide up to 3 screenshot images: dashboard, latency graph, billing view (1200x675).
  - Create 2 copy variants for A/B test (see below).
- Billing & trial flow
  - Define trial entitlement (free credits: e.g., $500 or 30-day capped usage).
  - Map marketplace trial to internal trial SKU and enable automated grant.
  - Confirm trial conversion webhook and test payload format.
  - Dry run: simulate trial grant -> invoice event -> internal usage mapping.
- Observability & telemetry
  - Add pilot tile to Redwood Console test dashboard.
  - Instrument token-level cost metrics and model choice logging.
  - Configure alerting for spike in error rate (> 1% request errors) and token burn anomalies.
- Go-live gating checklist (pre-launch smoke tests)
  - End-to-end flow: listing -> trial grant -> tenant created -> first inference returns successfully.
  - Billing event produced and received by Finance test webhook.
  - Tile copy verified in staging and region-specific language checks done.
  - Legal confirm marketing usage rights for partner logos on tile.

Acceptance matrix (pass/fail items):
- Provisioning success: tenant created programmatically (pass) / manual steps needed (fail)
- Billing mapping verified: invoice line items match SKU (pass) / mismatch or missing fields (fail)
- Security sign-off: SOC2 artifacts provided and pen-test checklist cleared (pass) / outstanding (fail)

Sample tile copy variants (short + long):
- Variant A (concise, product-first):
  - Short title: "Redwood Inference — Predictable LLM serving"
  - Short desc: "High-throughput, low-latency inference for production apps — hosted or private."
  - Long desc: "Redwood Inference provides an inference platform built for production: predictable latency SLOs, cost controls via batching and caching, and deployment flexibility across hosted, dedicated, and private models. Ship LLM features with confidence — pin model versions, configure routing policies, and monitor cost at token granularity. Pilot includes $500 free credits and full access to the test tenant."
- Variant B (outcome-focused):
  - Short title: "Ship LLM features faster — with predictable costs"
  - Short desc: "Reduce per-token cost and latency risk while scaling inference in production."
  - Long desc: "Today’s apps need inference that’s not just fast but economical and reliable. Redwood combines a GPU-optimized serving runtime with intelligent batching, KV caching, and a deployment abstraction that works across hosted and on-prem environments. The pilot gives limited free credits, dedicated support, and onboarding help to validate integration and conversion economics."

UX notes for tile screenshots and assets:
- Prefer real console screenshots (annotated) over mockups.
- Annotate where customers will see cost breakdowns and per-route latency.
- Include a simple diagram for trial provisioning flow (listing -> grant -> tenant -> webhook).

Sample marketplace trial onboarding email (to users after they click trial on marketplace):
Subject: Welcome to your Redwood Inference pilot
Body: Hi <name>, thanks for starting a trial of Redwood Inference via <marketplace>. Your test tenant is ready (tenant id: <id>). We've granted $500 in credits, valid for 60 days. Quickstart steps: 1) Get API key in console -> 2) Try the example curl to run a 256-token generation -> 3) Open the pilot dashboard to check token spending. If you'd like a walkthrough, reply to this email and we'll book 20 minutes.

Operational runbook snippets (for first 72 hours):
- Daily check-in with partner engineering (standup) to review telemetry for errors and cost trends.
- Finance: reconcile trial grants every 48 hours.
- Legal: monitor partner marketing assets usage.
- Escalation: if error rate > 3% or billing mapping failure, pause the tile and notify GTM/Platform leads.

Edge cases & mitigation suggestions:
- Marketplace API propagation delays: schedule start-of-trial tests at 00:00 UTC to avoid regional caching hiccups.
- Trial abuse detection: add rate limits to new tenants and flag accounts that exhaust credits in < 1 hour.
- Regional availability: if partner requires APAC-only visibility, coordinate with infra for region pinning (cost + capacity implications).

Post-pilot readout (deliverables):
- Metrics: trial grants, first-API-call time distribution, trial-to-paid conversion, average token burn per trial.
- Qualitative: partner feedback, integration blockers, docs clarity issues.
- Recommendations: go/no-go on broad listing; required product changes and estimated effort.

Open questions (needs input):
- Finance: default internal SKU for pilot discounts vs manual credit grants?
- Legal: standard pilot addendum template for marketplace partners?
- Platform: can we automate tenant provisioning via marketplace webhook or do we prefer manual kickoff for first pilot?

Appendix: quick checklist for partner intake call
- Collect contact info (technical + billing).
- Confirm expected QPS and sequence lengths (typical prompt sizes).
- Ask about any regulated data concerns and required regions.
- Agree on pilot KPIs and cadence of check-ins.

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc intentionally concise — additional detail belongs in the Confluence Pilot Spec (linked above).
- Save final tile assets and the A/B results CSV in the shared GTM drive folder once the pilot completes.
